committee: CC Commission for Persons with Disabilities
overview: The Medford Commission for Persons with Disabilities operates under city ordinance to advocate for residents with disabilities and ensure equal access across municipal facilities, public spaces, and civic processes. The body monitors physical infrastructure upgrades, reviews transit and pedestrian accommodations, and coordinates annual public disability events. Archive records span five meetings between October 2024 and September 2026. At its most recent meeting, the commission prioritized intersections for audible pedestrian signal upgrades funded by a casino mitigation grant and reviewed municipal accessibility surveys.

threads.name: Annual Disability Fair
threads.summary: The commission initiated planning in late 2024 for a disability fair at the inclusive playground, tentatively targeting spring 2025 with donor-supported social activities. After scheduling dates in April and then May 2025, the body arranged for sensory quiet spaces, disabled speakers and artists, and American Sign Language interpreters. In late 2025, the commission began coordinating dates in May 2026 for the subsequent annual fair.

threads.name: City Hall facility and accessibility improvements
threads.summary: The commission monitored facility upgrades at City Hall, noting the addition of armchairs to chambers, lighting updates, elevator repairs, and new assistive listening equipment funded by ARPA. Director Frances Nwajei reported that fully accessible bathroom renovations moved into the design phase. By late 2025, staff reported that ADA-compliant restroom renovations were moving toward execution.

threads.name: Transit and pedestrian infrastructure
threads.summary: Members engaged in ongoing advocacy regarding local transit, focusing on wayfinding signage and accessibility at the West Medford commuter rail station, including an accessible ramp scheduled to open in March 2025. Discussions also encompassed sidewalk conditions, snow removal compliance, and transit services such as 'The Ride'. In September 2026, the commission reviewed candidate intersections with Traffic Director Todd Blake to prioritize ADA-compliant audible pedestrian signals financed by a casino mitigation grant.

threads.name: Election and polling place accessibility
threads.summary: In late 2024, the commission raised concerns regarding the setup of accessible voting machines and planned site visits with the Elections Commission to inspect equipment and poll worker training. A year later, Director Frances Nwajei shared an update from the elections department concerning machine calibration and testing. This prompted further commission discussion regarding alternative voting methods and continued poll worker training.

threads.name: Parks, schools, and public spaces
threads.summary: The body reviewed its role in consulting on accessible design for municipal play spaces, including McGlynn school play spaces and Carr Park. Updates in late 2025 confirmed ramp construction at the McGlynn School, Gaga pit access procedures, and an upcoming accessibility audit of the public library. Amanda Centrella also presented survey data on park barriers to guide the Open Space and Recreation Plan extension.

threads.name: Commission operations and administrative oversight
threads.summary: The commission regularly reviewed its powers under municipal ordinance to advocate for residents and promote equal participation in civic affairs. Administrative actions included shifting fall meetings to combined December sessions each year, reviewing Open Meeting Law compliance, and tracking commissioner stipends. In 2026, the body also monitored Institute for Human Centered Design municipal surveys while addressing concerns over digital communication accessibility.
